identity.name: Navitimer B01 Chronograph 43
identity.one_liner: The 43mm steel flagship of Breitling's slide-rule pilot chronograph, built around the in-house B01 movement.

provenance_events.description: Breitling launches the Navitimer in 1952 — the first watch with a circular slide rule bezel, designed for pilots. The AOPA (Aircraft Owners and Pilots Association) endorsement turns the Navitimer into the most-cited pilot's watch of the 1950s-60s.

narrative.story: Breitling introduced the Navitimer in 1952 for members of the Aircraft Owners and Pilots Association, adapting the slide-rule bezel from its 1940s Chronomat into a tool for computing airspeed, fuel burn, and unit conversions in flight. The 2019 redesign dropped the interim "Navitimer 1" branding and paired the 43mm case with Breitling's in-house B01 chronograph movement, making AB0138 the collection's core steel model.
narrative.collector_notes: Dial color and strap (leather vs. steel bracelet) are the main configuration variables within this reference family; bracelet versions carry a meaningfully higher price than leather-strap versions.
